CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Add a wait for vblanks during atomic_commit Originally, drm/mediatek did not wait for vblanks in atomic_commit to avoid blocking page flips on legacy cursor ioctl updates. However, this was not necessary, thanks to upstream commit a987cb3c04cf ("drm/atomic-helpers: Recover full cursor plane behaviour"), which uses a special legacy_cursor_update flag to skip actually waiting for vblanks when handling legacy cursor updates. Here is the atomic update flow: drm_atomic_helper_swap_state(drm, state); drm_atomic_helper_commit_modeset_disables(drm, state); drm_atomic_helper_commit_modeset_enables(drm, state); drm_atomic_helper_commit_planes(drm, state, true); drm_atomic_helper_wait_for_vblanks(drm, state); drm_atomic_state_free(state); The wait_for_vblanks means we can really free the atomic state (and thereby unreference the old FB) in state_free, since we are sure it is no longer onscreen [1]. Furthermore, it is required that the driver only permit one page flip per crtc vblank. [1] - well, at least we can for page flips. For the asynchronous legacy cursor ioctl we still need to hold a reference to the old FB past drm_atomic_state_free(), and free it later in a dedicated unreference worker that is triggered by vblank. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: crtc: Remove cmdq_work and rework unreference work Previously, the command queue could only send one cmdq_rec per vblank. This limited the drm driver to only issue one atomic update per vblank. This is correct behavior for page flips, but it meant that the driver could not perform a legacy cursor ioctl and page flip in the same vblank, since that would require to atomic updates. Instead, the display driver collected commands from plane updates (primary and cursor) into "cmdq_pending" variables. The driver would then issue a single cmdq_rec with a wait of vblank to apply all pending changes to both primary and cursor planes. To ensure that this cmdq_rec was issued before vblank, the RDMA line interrupt was used to trigger an irq at 80% of frame duration. This irq would then schedule the cmdq work to actually create and submit the cmdq_rec to the command queue. The major disadvantage of this scheme, is that using the line irq throws away 20% of each frame. That is, if a page flip is requested after the line irq but before vblank, it would not get applied at the next vblank, instead it would be queued up and must wait as long as 120% of a frame period before it appearing on screen. Likewise, this would actually reduce frame rate, as userspace would also have to wait before it could submit the next page flip. To fix this, the command queue was updated to chain together atomic commits and apply them en masse at vblank. Therefore, the drm driver need no longer need to use the RDMA line irq to carefully time and apply cmdq_rec at 80% of frame duration. This patch removes the cmdq worker, and instead directly submits the cmdq_rec in atomic_flush. Furthermore, it starts the cmdq_rec in atomic_begin, and adds mtk_drm_crtc_plane_update to allow planes to request the crtc reprogram the display pipe components during atomic_update/disable(). Also, rather than tracking pending state in the struct mtk_drm_crtc, just use the struct drm_atomic_state, which already contains all of the information we need to know. In particular, during an atomic commit, the old drm_atomic_state holds a references to the old framebuffer that is coming ofscreen, that we will want to unreference once the flip is complete. For page flips an atomic commit is truly blocking - mtk_atomic_complete explicitly waits for the next vblank to confirm that a pending operation has completed before returning, and only one page flip is allowed per crtc per vblank. However, things get more complicated when dealing with the asynchronous legacy cursor. In order to possibly multiple cursor updates and page flips in a single vblank, there is a special "legacy_cursor_update" check that will skip waiting for vblank during an atomic cursor update. In other words, mtk_atomic_complete() finishes before it is confirmed that the update has really happened. If the cursor update is a cursor *disable* this means mtk_atomic_complete will finish while the old cursor FB is still being scanned out. However, once mtk_atomic_complete() finishes, the DRM core & userspace are free to drop all of their references on the cursor FB, which could lead to iommu faults. To avoid this, the current mtk_crtc layer takes an extra reference on each FB, and then uses a complicated scheme to manually track the state of FBs (new/onscreen/fb) to ensure that last reference is only dropped once the FB is truly no longer onscreen. The scheme uses a work, because the signal indicating that the FB is offscreen is handled in an interrupt handler, and unreferencing framebuffers is forbidden in atomic (or isr) context. This patch uses the information already stored in the drm_atomic_state itself to keep track of the "old FB" that should be freed. To ensure this information is available in the special case where we want to unreference and FB but mtk_atomic_complete() doesn't wait for vblank, we use a kref to pin the atomic state until it is released by both mtk_atomic_complete(), and by the unreference worker. The unreference worker is moved from the crtc layer up to the mtk_drv layer, since it is now unreferencing the whole drm_atomic_state, not just the old FB. Cleaning up the old RDMA line interrupt is left for a follow-up patch. This is correct behavior for page flips, but it meant that the driver could not perform a legacy cursor ioctl and page flip in the same vblank, since that would require to atomic updates. The driver would then issue a single cmdq_rec with a wait of vblank to apply all pending changes to both primary and cursor planes. To ensure that this cmdq_rec was issued before vblank, the RDMA line interrupt was used to trigger an irq at 80% of frame duration. This irq would then schedule the cmdq work to actually create and submit the cmdq_rec to the command queue. The major disadvantage of this scheme, is that using the line irq throws away 20% of each frame. That is, if a page flip is requested after the line irq but before vblank, it would not get applied at the next vblank, instead it would be queued up and must wait as long as 120% of a frame period before it appearing on screen. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Add comp prepare/unprepare callbacks Add display pipe component prepare/unprepare callbacks. These callbacks will be called when enabling/disabling their corresponding CRTC, and can be used to perform any functions required for a component before (prepare) accessing its registers via the cmdq, or after (unprepare) the last cmdq record has completed. In particular, the 'unprepare' callback is used for the encoder component to ensure the pixel clock is enabled until the cmdq has successfully completed the (possibly concatenated) stop operation. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Remove 'flip complete' completion The cmdq will now concatenate multiple cmdq_recs. In particular, during mtk_crtc_ddp_hw_fini(), the 'stop' command will now be appended to all pending page flip/cursor movements. Thus, the cmdq_rec_flush() after 'stop' becomes a synchronization point, which guarantees that any and all pending cmdq transactions have completed. Therefore, the 'completion' object, which was attempting to do the same thing, is now redundant. Furthermore, the completion didn't actually work, since it could only guarantee that a single pending transaction was complete; it does not actually properly handle concatenation. As a side-effect, we must also move the drm_crtc_vblank_off() after 'stop', to ensure that we still process any final pending vblanks prepended to 'stop'. Lastly, move drm_crtc_vblank_on() inside mtk_crtc_ddp_hw_init() for symmetry. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Only block updates to CRTCs that have a pending update Currently we use a single mutex to allow only a single atomic update at a time. In truth, though, we really only want to ensure that only a single atomic update is allowed per CRTC. In other words, for each atomic update, we only block if there is a pending update for the CRTCs involved, and don't block if there are only pending updates for other CRTCs. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Synchronize access to cmdq_vblank_event and cmdq_needs_event It is possible on an SMP system for CPU0 executing the ddp_cmdq_cb isr to read the new value for cmdq_needs_event (1) and an old value for cmdq_vblank_event (NULL) leading to an OOPs in drm_crtc_send_vblank_event(). Plug this situation using a pair of memory barriers. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Bypass atomic helpers for cursor updates Moving the driver to atomic helpers regressed cursor responsiveness, because cursor updates need their own atomic commits, which have to be serialized with other commits, that might include fence waits. To avoid this, in certain conditions, we can bypass the atomic helpers for legacy cursor update IOCTLs. Currently the conditions are: - no asynchronous mode setting commit pending, - no asynchronous commit that updates the cursor plane is pending. With the above two conditions met, we know that the manual cursor state update will not conflict with any scheduled update. CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: rockchip: Update dmc volts and idle states This lowers the voltages for 800 and 928MHz for the dmc. It also disables some of the idle states for 800+MHz since those were causing ripple on the center logic rail. The ripple was causing issues even with the increased voltage. This fixes the problem without the need to increase the voltage as much at 928MHz.
